evals.name: three-inline-comments-csv-export
evals.prompt: The attached brief gives three findings from your review of a colleague's pull request. Write the three inline comments you will post for Ivan, one per finding, in the order given, separated by a line containing only `---`. Return only the comments. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output: Three inline comments, each opening on its own finding at its `file:line` or symbol, each carrying one ask graded to its severity, none asserting a failure the reviewer did not observe, and no two sharing an opening construction, closing move, or length profile.

expectations.text: Each comment opens with the finding as a plain declarative anchored on its `file:line` or the backticked symbol (`list(query.all())`, the unused `json` and `Optional` imports, `fmt` versus `format`); an optional one-line finding title naming the acceptable outcome may precede the blocker comment, but there is no topic label, severity-only heading, or 'I noticed' lead-in.

Each comment makes exactly one ask whose form matches its severity: 'Please' plus an imperative for the unbounded `list(query.all())` read, 'Let's' or a one-line drop for the unused imports, and a declinable question or a first-person lean for the `fmt` naming.

The blocker comment states what the code does (the whole result set held in memory before writing) and what would expose it (the 40-million-row table), without asserting that the handler fails, failed, or crashes, since the reviewer ran nothing.
The three comments do not share an opening construction, a closing move, or a length profile, and none ends with an 'Also, ...' afterthought.

evals.name: unrun-test-outcome-duration-parser
evals.prompt: The attached brief gives one finding from your review of a colleague's pull request, which you read but did not run. Write the single inline comment you will post for Ivan. Return only the comment. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output: One comment that states what `utils/duration.py:28` does as a plain declarative, predicts the test's outcome with a modal or a condition rather than asserting it, and asks for the multiplier fix with 'Please' since it blocks merge.

expectations.text: The comment states as a plain declarative, anchored on `utils/duration.py:28`, that the hours branch multiplies by 60 (so `"1h30m"` yields 1860 seconds), because the code in the diff establishes that.

The comment describes the outcome of `test_parse_duration_mixed_units` with a modal or a condition ('should fail as written', 'will fail once run') and never states that the test fails, failed, or is red, nor that CI failed, since the reviewer ran nothing and CI has not reported.
The comment makes one ask, phrased with 'Please' plus an imperative, to change the hours multiplier to 3600, and says why that closes the failure path.

evals.name: re-review-summary-new-head
evals.prompt: The attached brief describes the state of your prior findings on a colleague's pull request after the author pushed a new head. Write the review summary Ivan posts with the re-review. Return only the summary. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output: A summary that opens with what the new head resolved, states the one remaining finding at its `file:line` with a single ask, names the residual gaps, and keeps review confidence separate from merge readiness despite green checks and a bot approval.

expectations.text: The summary opens by naming what the new head resolved (the `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` cap and the token redaction) before anything else, without restating the original comments at length.

The summary states the unchanged retry at `api/upload.py:64` as the remaining finding with exactly one ask, phrased as a blocker, to limit retries to `httpx.TransportError` or an equivalently narrow transient class.

The summary does not call the PR mergeable, approved, or ready on the strength of green checks or the bot's approval; it names the skipped 413 integration test and the uninspected `openapi.json` as residual gaps.

evals.name: credit-and-nit-error-path
evals.prompt: The attached brief gives two findings from your review of a colleague's pull request. Write the two inline comments you will post for Ivan, in order, separated by a line containing only `---`. Return only the comments. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output: Two comments: the first credits the decorator move only because that credit carries the leak finding and then asks for the fixed message with 'Please'; the second is a labeled nit with one declinable ask and no second request.

expectations.text: In the first comment, any credit for moving validation into the decorator appears because it sets up the finding (every handler now hits the new error path) and comes before the flag; there is no freestanding praise in either comment.

The first comment names the leak at `svc/handlers.py:31` (the absolute schema path in the response) with its consequence, and makes one 'Please' ask for a fixed client message with `exc` logged server-side.
The second comment is labeled as a nit or non-blocking, anchors on `svc/handlers.py:19`, makes one declinable ask to type `schema` as `Schema`, and adds no further request.

evals.name: pre-post-edit-pass-batch
evals.prompt: The attached brief contains three drafted inline comments and the facts behind them. Run the pre-post edit pass over the batch and return the three revised comments, in order, separated by a line containing only `---`. Return only the comments. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output: Three revised comments that keep every `file:line` and exactly one ask each, turn the unrun CI claim into a modal or a condition, strike 'I noticed', 'That said', 'worth noting', and the 'Also, ...' tails, judge each dash by its usage, and no longer share an opening construction.

expectations.text: The first comment no longer asserts that the zero TTL 'fails in CI'; it states what `cache/store.py:57` does and gives the outcome a modal or a condition, since the reviewer ran nothing and CI has not reported.

No revised comment contains 'I noticed', 'That said', 'worth noting', or an 'Also, ...' tail, and every remaining em dash has been judged by its usage: a parenthetical one is unspaced, a spaced one is a non-parenthetical usage, and any dash that was not the best structure is replaced by a colon, parentheses, a semicolon, or a new sentence.

Each revised comment keeps its `file:line` and exactly one ask (the `None` default, dropping the import, the `_evict_stale_keys` rename), drops the extra requests about the schema, the docstring, and the test, and the three no longer open with the same 'In `file:line`' construction.
